answer: Joining burns rather than stakes: the fee is destroyed, so it never returns to the attacker, and the burn echoes permanently in the ledger. Price curves with joins since the last comet, a rare beacon, so a batch minted in a quiet window pays far more per identity. Each newcomer must bridge to the previous joiner by referencing its hash, and a consecutive run counts as one seat until the bridge ages three epochs. A farm therefore burns k times at rising prices and collects a single seat, while honest agents arrive one at a time and pay the base price.
